summary: Current 1957 L-4 tower on Meadow Peak replaced two earlier lookouts dating to 1928; staffed until the 1990s, NHLR-listed in 2000, and now a Forest Service rental.

access.note: High-clearance 4WD recommended; rough mountain road with loose rock.

visit.trail_note: Reached by rough 4WD road, not a maintained hiking trail.

events.note: Current 10-foot L-4 tower built by contractor Leonard Sheffield for about $6,299.
First staffed by Mr. and Mrs. Dave Griffith.
Last staffed in the 1990s per Recreation.gov; NHLR (surveyed circa 2000) says unstaffed for at least 10 years.
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 344 on May 12, 2000.

evidence.supports: cupola cabin built 1928, 15' L-4 in 1936, current tower built 1957, contractor and cost
evidence.quote: The first lookout was a cupola cabin built in 1928, the second lookout was built in 1936 it was a 15' L-4 style lookout and the the current lookout was built in 1957 as a 10' L-4 style for $6299.
Leonard Sheffield was the contractor and had 3 Forest Service employees to help with the build.
The lookout was last staffed in the 1990's and was placed on the National Historic Lookout Register in 2000.

evidence.supports: built 1957 by Forest Service, Griffiths first staff in 1958
evidence.quote: Meadow Mountain is now staffed by the Montana State Division Division of Forestry in cooperation with the U.S. Forest Service which built the structure in 1957. The first people to staff the lookout when it went in service in 1958 were Mr. and Mrs. Dave Griffith.

evidence.supports: unstaffed ~10 years as of 2000 registration, condition
evidence.quote: Weather beaten, some vandalism, but less than would be expected. Open but no longer staffed for at least 10 years.
The lookout is typically open from mid-June through late September. High clearance 4 wheel drive vehicles with off-road tires are required.

evidence.supports: cabin sleeps 4, no water/electricity, cell service available
evidence.quote: Meadow Peak lookout stands 10 feet tall and has a 225 square foot cabin, which is encircled by a catwalk. It sleeps four and comes furnished with two twin beds, both with mattresses.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Recreation.gov states the lookout was last staffed in the 1990s; the NHLR description, drafted around the 2000 registration, says it had gone unstaffed for 'at least 10 years', which points to the late 1980s. Both are consistent with staffing ending sometime in the late 1980s to 1990s, so the story says 'into the 1990s' rather than picking one exact year.

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com (source 3) corroborates the 1928/1936/1957 construction sequence but was not directly footnoted in the story since Recreation.gov already covers it in more detail; kept as a cross-check source. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the story had described the current cab as a '14-by-14-foot' tower; the Recreation.gov page actually gives a 225-square-foot cabin with no 14x14 dimension stated, so the story was corrected to match the source.
